headings.title: Introduction and Foundations of Dietary Counselling
headings.content: Dietary counselling is a collaborative process between a healthcare professional and a client to address nutrition-related concerns and establish healthy eating habits. Unlike simple meal planning, it requires active listening, behavioural change techniques, and cultural competence. The primary goal is to empower individuals to make informed dietary choices that prevent disease and manage existing health conditions. A common misconception in clinical practice is that counselling is merely telling a patient what to eat. Effective nutrition counselling assesses readiness to change and builds sustainable habits tailored to the patient's socioeconomic reality, especially within Nigerian communities where food availability and cultural practices heavily influence dietary intake.

headings.title: Individual Dietary Counselling
headings.content:
One-on-one dietary counselling provides personalized nutrition care tailored to a specific patient's physiological needs, lifestyle, and medical history. This private setting allows nurses and dietitians to discuss sensitive health issues such as weight management, eating disorders, or chronic disease self-care without privacy concerns.

- **Assessment**: Gathers detailed dietary recall, anthropometric measurements, and biochemical data.
- **Goal Setting**: Establishes realistic, patient-centered targets like reducing salt intake or increasing fiber.
- **Follow-up**: Monitors progress, evaluates adherence, and modifies the care plan as needed.

headings.title: Group Dietary Counselling
headings.content:
Group dietary counselling brings together individuals sharing similar health goals or conditions, such as diabetes support groups, antenatal nutrition classes, or weight-loss cohorts. This approach fosters peer support, shared experiences, and collective motivation, which can significantly enhance adherence.

| Feature | Individual Counselling | Group Counselling |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Privacy | High (one-on-one) | Low (shared environment) |
| Cost Efficiency | Lower per hour | Higher (reaches many at once) |
| Peer Support | Absent | High (shared experiences) |

headings.title: Therapeutic and Clinical Counselling
headings.content: Therapeutic nutrition counselling is an essential component of medical treatment for patients diagnosed with specific pathologies such as chronic kidney disease, severe malnutrition, diabetes mellitus, or cardiovascular disorders. The nurse works closely with dietitians and physicians to translate complex medical prescriptions into practical dietary modifications. For instance, a patient with renal failure requires strict restriction of potassium, sodium, and fluid intake. Therapeutic counselling ensures the patient understands the clinical consequences of non-adherence while finding palatable food substitutes to maintain adequate nutritional status.

headings.title: Preventive and Community Nutrition Counselling
headings.content: Preventive nutrition counselling focuses on population health, targeting healthy communities, schools, and vulnerable groups to prevent diet-related non-communicable diseases. Nurses in primary health care centers use this approach to educate nursing mothers on exclusive breastfeeding, weaning foods, and balanced diets using locally available food items. By addressing nutritional deficiencies before they manifest as clinical diseases, community counselling reduces the burden on secondary and tertiary healthcare facilities.

headings.title: Directive Versus Non-Directive Counselling Approaches
headings.content:
Counselling styles range along a continuum from counselor-centered to client-centered.

- **Directive Counselling**: The nurse takes an authoritative, expert role, providing clear instructions and specific meal plans. This works well for confused patients or acute clinical emergencies where immediate dietary changes are mandatory.
- **Non-Directive Counselling**: The nurse acts as a facilitator, asking open-ended questions and guiding the client to discover their own solutions. This approach builds long-term autonomy and is effective for chronic lifestyle modifications.

headings.title: Digital and Tele-Counselling in Modern Dietary Practice
headings.content: Modern technology has transformed dietary counselling through tele-health platforms, mobile applications, and SMS reminders. Tele-counselling bridges geographical gaps, allowing nurses to monitor and advise patients living in remote rural areas without requiring physical clinic attendance. While it improves accessibility and convenience, nurses must remain mindful of digital literacy barriers, unreliable internet connectivity, and the loss of non-verbal cues during virtual sessions.
